questions.prompt: A product team wants people to enjoy their video feed more. What's a good ML framing?

options.text: Use the largest neural network available
Predict how likely a user is to watch a video substantially, then rank candidates by that score

questions.explanation: Framing turns the business goal into a concrete prediction (watching most of a video, as a proxy for enjoyment) and an output (a ranking).

questions.prompt: Only 0.1% of transactions are fraudulent. Which metrics should you report for a fraud classifier?

options.text: Precision and recall at the chosen threshold

questions.explanation: Always predicting "not fraud" is 99.9% accurate and useless. Precision, recall and the PR curve reflect performance on the rare class; losses avoided is the business metric.

questions.prompt: You train a churn model on two years of data. How should you split training and test data?

options.text: By time: train on older data and test on the most recent months
Test on the training data to save time

questions.explanation: A random split lets the model peek at the future, so offline results look better than reality. A time split mimics how the model will be used.

questions.prompt: Offline metrics look great, but the model performs worse in production. Training used a nightly batch feature, while serving computes it from live data. What is this?

options.text: Training–serving skew; fix it by computing features once and serving the same values, for example through a feature store
Overfitting, fixed by adding more layers

questions.explanation: Different feature logic in training and serving means the model sees inputs it wasn't trained on. Sharing feature definitions and values removes the gap.

questions.prompt: A new ranking model beats the baseline offline. What should happen before it serves all users?

options.text: Shadow mode on live traffic to check latency and errors
An A/B test on a random slice of users, comparing the online metric and guardrails
A gradual rollout with a fast rollback
Nothing: offline wins guarantee online wins

questions.explanation: Offline metrics are a proxy. Shadow mode catches operational problems, the A/B test measures real impact, and gradual rollout limits the damage if something was missed.
